identification.summary: Volga Flood is Microsoft's name for a Russia-linked influence-operation actor, formerly tracked as Storm-1841 and also called Rybar in Microsoft Threat Analysis Center (MTAC) coverage [S1][S2]. Secondary reporting says the actor ran social media channels posing as a grassroots military blogger and targeted US audiences on immigration in 2024 [S2][S3]. The State Department separately accused the Russian company Rybar LLC of US election interference in October 2024 [S4][S5].
identification.firstObserved: Early 2024 (creation of Telegram and X accounts, per secondary reporting on MTAC) [S2]. The Rybar Telegram project itself predates this; its start date is not established in the sources gathered.
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Volga Flood (formerly Storm-1841); alias Rybar as reported in coverage of the MTAC report [S1][S2]. Do not merge with Ruza Flood (Doppelganger) or Storm-1516, which Microsoft lists as separate actors [S1][S3]. A search summary suggested the MTAC text mixes spellings of Ruza and Volga Flood; this is unverified and should be checked against the PDF.

attribution.sponsor: Microsoft describes Volga Flood as a Russia-linked influence actor; it does not, in the sources opened, name a specific Russian agency [S1][S2]. The US State Department stated that Rybar receives funding from Rostec, and was earlier funded by Yevgeniy Prigozhin, per news reports of the announcement [S4][S5]. The EU listed founder Mikhail Zvinchuk in June 2023 citing his membership of a Putin-established working group coordinating mobilization [S6].
attribution.confidence: Not stated in the sources gathered. Microsoft's linkage of Storm-1841 to the Rybar brand is as reported by media [S2]; the State Department's allegations are government allegations reported by press, not independently verified [S4][S5].
attribution.basis: Microsoft MTAC election report of 2024-09-17 (titled 'Russia leverages cyber proxies and Volga Flood assets in expansive influence efforts') [S1]; coverage of the State Department Rewards for Justice announcement [S4][S5]. The full MTAC PDF could not be opened.

objectives: Influence US political discourse ahead of the 2024 election, with Rybar-linked content focused on US immigration issues, per secondary reporting on MTAC [S2][S3]. The State Department alleged Rybar sought to exploit the Texas border immigration issue and spread pro-Russian propaganda via accounts such as 'TexasvsUSA', #HOLDTHELINE and #STANDWTHTEXAS [S4][S5].

targeting.notes: Targets are audiences and the US electoral environment, not networks. Rybar has also published military mapping content, for example a map of the EU force EUFOR exercise locations in Bosnia, per a search summary of detektor.ba reporting; not independently verified [S7].

capabilities.summary: Operates social media channels (Telegram, X) posing as a grassroots military blogger and spreads inflammatory content, per secondary reporting [S2]. Reported content includes a roughly 30-second AI-generated clip of immigrant 'zombies' at the US southern border [S2]. The State Department described use of an X channel and hashtag campaigns on the Texas border issue [S4][S5]. Microsoft's report also noted generative AI use across Russian influence actors [S1]. Rybar is described as a pro-war Telegram channel of 1.3 to 1.5 million subscribers founded by Mikhail Zvinchuk, a former Defense Ministry press service staffer [S8].

campaigns.name: Rybar-linked Telegram and X accounts targeting US immigration debate
campaigns.summary: Per secondary reporting on MTAC, the actor created Telegram and X accounts with inflammatory content, including an AI-generated 'zombie' border clip [S2].

campaigns.name: Microsoft MTAC election report 4
campaigns.summary: Microsoft published 'Russia leverages cyber proxies and Volga Flood assets in expansive influence efforts', naming Volga Flood (formerly Storm-1841) among Russian actors in the 2024 US election [S1][S2].

campaigns.name: State Department reward for Rybar information
campaigns.summary: Announced 2024-10-18 per press coverage dated 2024-10-18/19. Rewards for Justice offered up to $10 million for information on Rybar LLC and nine named individuals including Zvinchuk, alleging election interference via a 'TexasvsUSA' X channel and hashtags, and Rostec funding [S4][S5].

campaigns.name: UK sanctions on Rybar project members
campaigns.summary: UK expanded sanctions to ten more people tied to the Rybar project; reported dating differs across sources and needs checking against the UK list [S9].

campaigns.name: Zvinchuk detained and expelled from Montenegro
campaigns.summary: RFE/L and others report Zvinchuk was detained in Montenegro and ordered to leave, with authorities citing national security and disinformation fears; Rybar said it was filming at a monastery [S8].

diamond.adversary: Microsoft-tracked Russia-linked influence actor Volga Flood (ex Storm-1841), associated with the Rybar brand and founder Mikhail Zvinchuk; government funding links alleged by the State Department [S1][S2][S4].
diamond.capability: Fake grassroots military-blogger personas, Telegram and X channels, hashtag campaigns, and AI-generated video [S2][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Telegram and X accounts and channels (for example 'TexasvsUSA') [S2][S4]. Domains and hosting not identified in sources gathered.
diamond.victim: US electorate and online audiences on immigration issues; EU/NATO-related military audiences in other Rybar content [S2][S4][S7].
diamond.socioPolitical: 2024 US election influence context and Russia's war on Ukraine; Rybar sanctioned by EU, UK and Ukraine for role in the war effort [S1][S6][S9].
diamond.technology: Open social media platforms and generative AI tools used to scale persuasive content [S1][S2].

gaps: Microsoft's primary MTAC report (Election Report 4, 2024-09-17) could not be opened; all Microsoft statements here come from press coverage and search snippets [S1][S2].
Whether Microsoft considers Volga Flood identical to the Rybar organization or only an associated asset set is not confirmed.
Microsoft's attribution confidence and any named sponsor agency are not known.
UK and EU sanction dates and wording not verified against official lists; search summaries disagreed on the UK date [S6][S9].
Activity after the 2024 election, and whether Microsoft renamed or merged this cluster since, is not established.
Overlap with Ruza Flood (Doppelganger) and Storm-1516 is unresolved; keep clusters separate.
Rybar Africa activity and Wagner-era links were searched but not confirmed for this actor.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is the information environment: Telegram and X audiences and military-themed channels that service members and allies may follow. STEP 2: The actor blends military-blogger credibility with political messaging and AI content, and is tied by US allegations to state-linked funding [S2][S4]. STEP 3: Pattern is persona accounts, hashtag campaigns, and AI-generated video on divisive topics such as immigration [S2][S4]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued narrative amplification on US domestic issues and Ukraine war topics. MDCOA is use of the military-blog brand to publish location or exercise details about NATO or US forces, as with the reported EUFOR map [S7], to enable targeting or discredit operations. Candidate indicators: new Rybar-branded accounts on X, coordinated hashtag bursts, AI-generated border or military clips, and maps of exercises.
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track Rybar-branded channels for posts about exercises or US/allied force locations and feed to OPSEC and public affairs [S7]. (2) Authorities: this is an influence, not a network intrusion actor, so response sits with public affairs, information operations and law enforcement/State rather than cyber defense alone [S4]. (3) Mission assurance: remind personnel of OPSEC and social media risk around exercises. (4) Coordination: share indicators with allied partners given EU and UK sanctions interest [S6][S9].
